To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the LULC map of the canal command area of Lower Chenab Canal system, Pakistan, was successfully generated from LANDSAT 7 images using supervised classification and the estimated canal water deficit for Rabi season 2010 11 is 33% 72%.
the LULC maps of the command areas of the three distributaries were developed and the irrigation water demand for the cropped area was estimated for the Rabi seasons.
the LULC maps of the canal command area were prepared with an accuracy of 84 and 86%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of canal deficit water using remote sensing and GIS.
the estimation of LULC in the canal command areas using the remote sensing and GIS techniques.
the estimation of CWD using remote sensing and GIS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CWD in the irrigated areas of the lower Chenab Canal command area has been estimated using satellite remote sensing and GIS.
the LULC mapping using LANDSAT data and the estimation of CWD using GIS is very effective and efficient tool to assess the canal water demand and deficit in the command area.
the satellite remote sensing and GIS can play a significant role in the estimation of CWD in the canal command areas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LULC map of irrigated command areas of the lower Chenab canals was prepared and canal water deficit was estimated.
the satellite remote sensing and GIS can be used for the estimation of LULC and irrigation water deficit in canal command area.
the remote sensing and GIS can be effectively used for the estimation of CWD and the results can help in improving the canal water management system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the CWD in the irrigated area of lower Chenab canal is very high and it can be managed by the proper management of water resources and the implementation of appropriate water saving techniques in the irrigated areas.
the remote sensing and GIS based LULC mapping can be a useful tool in the estimation of canal irrigation water deficit.
the LULC map of the canal command area is a useful tool for the estimation of CWD and the identification of the area where the water deficit exists.
